Two ways to watch the bats from the water
The bat cruise question, answered straight
caption: Boat cruise or kayak for the Congress Avenue bats? A boat wins on comfort. A kayak wins on quiet, closeness and the view from under the arches. Here's the honest split. #austinbats #ladybirdlake #austinkayaktours #congressavenuebridge

slides.kicker: Seeing the bats from the water?
slides.headline: Big boat or kayak? Depends what you want.
slides.body: Both put you on Lady Bird Lake at dusk. They're very different evenings. Here's the honest split.

slides.headline: Nobody in your group wants to paddle
slides.body: Seats, a railing, zero effort. Good for mobility limits, dressy outfits, or anyone set on staying dry.

slides.headline: You want to sit at water level
slides.body: You're low on the lake near the bridge, looking straight up when the colony comes out.

slides.headline: A kayak is quiet
slides.body: No engine, no loudspeaker. You hear paddles, traffic on the bridge and people cheering above you.

slides.headline: Smaller group, more room
slides.body: Anna M. called her sunset group "small and intimate, which made it feel really special." Sizes vary by night.

slides.headline: Real talk: you paddle
slides.body: Easy pace, flat water, about two hours. Expect wet shoes and light arm work. A land lesson comes first.

slides.headline: Room to drift on your own
slides.body: Sheila S. liked that guides "gave us the freedom to freely explore the area."

slides.headline: Under the arches, not behind a railing
slides.body: From a kayak you look up through the bridge. The sky is the backdrop, not the back of someone's head.

slides.headline: Want comfort: boat. Want close and quiet: kayak.
slides.body: Either way, go before early November. The colony leaves with the cold fronts.

slides.kicker: Send this to whoever's planning bat night
slides.headline: If it's the kayak, we saved you a seat
slides.body: Guided sunset bat tours on Lady Bird Lake. Book at austinkayaktours.com.
